title: Ang 1070–1086: Ram Das and Arjan's Solhe
hookLine: the fourth and fifth Gurus' Solhe
tomorrow: can six days of Maru fit in one breath?

cards: Someone says something cutting, right to your face, and everyone hears. There's a split second where you choose: clap back, go silent, or something else.

Here's one question, then, for a wisdom day: what do you say when someone mocks you? Guru Arjan has an answer in these pages. And it turns out a neighbor tradition, in its own book, gives a strikingly close one.

teach.b: From ang 1070 come more Solhe: first by Guru Ram Das, the fourth Guru, then by Guru Arjan, the fifth. In one of Guru Arjan's, on ang 1083, he speaks straight to a Muslim listener, in that listener's own words for God.

teach.h: O SERVANT OF ALLAH, OF KHUDA.
teach.b: It opens, in paraphrase: O servant of Allah, the unknowable, of Khuda, let go of the world's busy tangles.
Become like the dust under the feet of the fakirs, a traveler on the way. That's the Guru's answer to pride, and to the mocker too: you don't need to win the moment. You're passing through.
The Qur'an, describing the faithful, says this: they are those "who walk upon the earth modestly, and when the foolish ones address them answer: Peace."
Shared: the humble walk, and an answer that refuses to fight on the mocker's terms. Neither is weakness. It takes courage to say one calm word and keep walking.
And one honest difference. For Muslims, the Qur'an is God's own word, revealed to the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him. For Sikhs, the Guru Granth Sahib is itself the living Guru.
Two books, two homes, and on this one question, a very similar path.

how: The Maru Solhe of Guru Ram Das and Guru Arjan are sung in kirtan and read in order in a complete reading of the Guru Granth Sahib.

s: Guru Arjan's hymns only ever use Punjabi names for God
this Solha speaks to a Muslim listener as a servant of Allah, of Khuda.
the Qur'an says the faithful answer the foolish with: Peace
they 'walk upon the earth modestly' and answer: Peace (25:63, Pickthall).
since both say it, Sikh and Muslim teaching are basically the same
they share this humble walk; Muslims receive the Qur'an as God's word, Sikhs follow the Guru Granth Sahib as Guru.

games.q: in a meeting, a coworker mocks how you said a word, and a few people laugh. by Guru Arjan's 'traveler' and the Qur'an's 'peace', what fits?
o: one calm word, then keep going; you don't need to win the moment.
mock him back so the room knows not to try it again.
never speak up again; being humble means you don't matter.
games.why: both texts picture a humble walker who answers without fighting on the mocker's terms. that's not silence or weakness: it takes nerve.

practice: If you can, stand and take a slow walk across the room, letting each foot land softly, like a traveler with nowhere to prove anything. If you're sitting, just press each foot gently into the floor in turn.
Step, and peace; step, and peace.
